parsed.basis: Herat, in western Afghanistan near the Iran border, is governed under the Taliban's nationwide regime, which provides no legal protection based on sexual orientation or gender identity and treats same-sex conduct and gender nonconformity as moral crimes punishable by flogging, imprisonment and, under Sharia-based provisions, death. The Promotion of Virtue and Prevention of Vice Law requires moral surveillance, and reports document beatings, sexual abuse in custody, arbitrary detention and public punishments, with visibly transgender people facing the gravest risks of exploitation and violence. Although Herat city has historically been a more urban, educated and ethnically diverse centre than some rural areas, there is no local legal exception, protective institution or tourism-based tolerance that changes how discovery would be handled by Taliban authorities.
